advisories.title: macos-product-build is the only selector branch in the contract that names no observation interface and no failure mode, while the contract's own standard makes both grammar
advisories.observation: The scheme is one sentence: 'macOS product-build string as Apple publishes it, after Unicode NFC and trim of leading/trailing ASCII whitespace.' It has no schemeId, no canonicalIdentifier object, no named source interface, and no absent/unobservable refusal rule. Every sibling selector branch in this contract supplies all of that. linux-distro-userspace names os-release(5), names the exact keys ID and VERSION_ID, puts /usr/lib/os-release explicitly OUT of scope, excludes uname -r by name, and states 'If VERSION_ID is absent the profile refuses.' filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution names struct statfs.f_fstypename with 'No other interface' for macOS, names the fs_vfstype field after the '-' separator for Linux with 'Not a numeric field ordinal. Linux struct statfs.f_type is not the token', and gives refusal on unobservable/missing/ambiguous. I grepped the whole 279431-byte subject: sw_vers, ProductBuildVersion, ProductVersion, SystemVersion, kern.osversion, kern.osproductversion, plist and CoreServices each occur zero times. The three occurrences of uname are all exclusions inside the Linux scheme. macos-product-build is named in exactly two sentences in the file, its own definition and the schemeBinding line.
advisories.whyItMatters: This contract treats 'which interface produces the token' as part of the selector grammar, not as a packet choice, and /platformProfile/selectorGrammar/supportedVersionOrBuildSelector/serialization binds the later packet: 'The later packet chooses values inside this language and MUST NOT mint range or scheme semantics.' Under the contract's own theory the macOS observation interface is therefore a grammar element, and it is absent. A population packet author supplying it would be minting scheme semantics the grammar forbids them to mint.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Not introduced by this successor. /platformProfile/selectorGrammar is not on the v46 closed roster and is byte-identical to platform-tcb-contract.v45; editing it would itself have been a roster violation requiring a roster amendment. The successor makes no false statement about it. This lineage's own calibration for a carried-unchanged asymmetry is ADVISORY, as recorded at CLAUDE-V45-A2. Equality is also not indeterminate in practice: EXACT-BUILD.equality is 'byte-exact canonicalIdentifier after that scheme's named normalization', the macOS named normalization is closed at NFC plus trim, and wildcardRejected and emptyRejected both hold, so a value once chosen compares determinately.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional for the successor; load-bearing for the C4-c grade. A future round that intends an unreserved application-grade grant should give macos-product-build the same three elements its siblings carry: a named source interface, a named exclusion of the near neighbour (ProductVersion is not this field), and an absent/unobservable refusal rule.
advisories.notAFinding: This advisory does not populate a selector value, does not name a macOS build string, and does not invent an interface. It records the shape of the gap only.

gradeRuling.questionRestated: Is platform-tcb-contract.v46, as bytes, acceptable at application grade - T2-02's application-grade acceptance with no express reservation - as DR-126's design-contract candidate for the selector grammar, with selector values and per-OS profiles remaining RESERVED?
reservationSweep: The macOS version/build branch of the selector grammar is not closed to the standard the contract applies to its other selector branches, and a byte must be added there before an unreserved application-grade grant.
I sustain the grammar's application-grade fitness for the filesystem member and for the Linux version/build member; I reserve it for macos-product-build only.
This reservation is confined to /platformProfile/selectorGrammar/supportedVersionOrBuildSelector/identifierSchemes/macos-product-build and reaches no other path in the subject.
NOT SUSTAINED judges the higher, newly posed bar of an unreserved application-grade grant over the carried grammar, which the macos-product-build branch does not yet meet.

A future round that intends an unreserved application-grade grant should give macos-product-build the same three elements its siblings carry: a named source interface, a named exclusion of the near neighbour (ProductVersion is not this field), and an absent/unobservable refusal rule.
reasons: The grade question sets the bar at acceptance with no express reservation, and defines NOT SUSTAINED as the answer if any byte of the subject would need to change before that grant. One byte-level addition is needed, so the honest answer is NOT SUSTAINED.

This contract makes the observation interface part of the selector grammar rather than a packet choice. It does so explicitly for every other selector branch: linux-distro-userspace names os-release(5) and the keys ID and VERSION_ID, puts /usr/lib/os-release OUT of scope, excludes uname -r by name, and refuses when VERSION_ID is absent; filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution names struct statfs.f_fstypename with 'No other interface' for macOS and the fs_vfstype field after the '-' separator for Linux, excludes struct statfs.f_type and numeric field ordinals by name, and refuses when the token is unobservable, missing or ambiguous.

macos-product-build carries none of that. It is a single sentence, 'macOS product-build string as Apple publishes it, after Unicode NFC and trim of leading/trailing ASCII whitespace', with no source interface, no near-neighbour exclusion and no refusal rule. Searching all 279431 bytes, the identifiers by which macOS actually publishes that string do not occur: sw_vers, ProductBuildVersion, ProductVersion, SystemVersion, kern.osversion, kern.osproductversion, plist and CoreServices are each absent.

The gap is load-bearing rather than cosmetic because supportedVersionOrBuildSelector.serialization binds the later packet with 'The later packet chooses values inside this language and MUST NOT mint range or scheme semantics.' A packet author populating the macOS profile must decide which interface and which key produce the token. Under the contract's own theory that decision is scheme semantics, which the grammar forbids them to mint, so the packet cannot be written from this grammar alone without either overstepping that prohibition or amending the grammar first.

The scope of the grant makes this decisive rather than deferrable. The grant sought is for the selector grammar precisely while values stay RESERVED, so the grammar is the whole of what is being graded. An unreserved application-grade grant would assert that a population packet can be built against this grammar without inventing anything, and for one of the two osFamily values in osFamilyEnum that is not yet true.

The repair is small, additive and available to a later round: give macos-product-build the three elements its siblings carry, a named source interface, a named exclusion of the near neighbour, and an absent-or-unobservable refusal rule. It touches one path and needs no new selector value, so the C4-c grade is reachable at the next successor rather than blocked.

Nothing else in the subject defeats the grade. The identity rule, the four-field signedEntry, the loader-trace and measured-boot machinery, the resolution predicate, the negative tests and the filesystem selector are all closed to application-grade rigor, and the reservations the question itself grants - selector values RESERVED, per-OS profiles RESERVED, populatedTables and ikconfigParserVectors RESERVED as G22 evidence - are premises of the question rather than reservations of my verdict, so I do not count them in the sweep above.
This ruling is a reviewer judgment only. It does not open D-056 Class A, does not SATISFY DR-126, does not QUALIFY G22, does not populate any table, and is not a binds value.
gradeRuling.relationToVerdict: The ACCEPT and the NOT SUSTAINED are consistent and answer different questions. ACCEPT judges this successor's own bytes: v46 carries platform-tcb-contract.v45 faithfully, invents nothing, holds every reservation field, and states nothing its bytes contradict, so it has no blocker and no SHOULD-FIX. NOT SUSTAINED judges the higher, newly posed bar of an unreserved application-grade grant over the carried grammar, which the macos-product-build branch does not yet meet. The condition is inherited from platform-tcb-contract.v45 on a path the v46 closed roster deliberately does not touch, which is why it is an advisory in the successor and a reservation at grade.
